# The Executive

## By the end of today

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
You will be able to explain why a republic needs an executive strong enough to secure rights and why that same concentrated force is why we constrain it.
:::

## Where this fits

Congress writes policy.

The executive **implements** it — with force if needed.

That is both the point and the danger.

## Necessary Leviathan

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.7em;"}
Rights on paper mean little if no one can enforce them.
:::

## Defender of rights

![Three branches and their core powers](../../assets/3_branches_powers.jpg){fig-alt="Diagram of legislative, executive, and judicial powers" width="80%"}

## What the office actually does

- Execute the laws
- Command the armed forces
- Appoint officers
- Pardon
- Receive ambassadors

## Take Care

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
"He shall take Care that the Laws be faithfully executed."
:::

## Vesting

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
"The executive Power shall be vested in a President of the United States of America."
:::

## One person, not a committee

Energy in the executive was Hamilton's argument.

A single accountable officer can act quickly.

That is also why the office is dangerous.

## Despoiler of rights

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.7em;"}
The same hand that enforces rights can violate them.
:::

## Remember the king

![King as fused lawgiver, enforcer, and judge](../../assets/king_roles.jfif){fig-alt="Diagram of a king combining lawgiver, enforcer, and judge" width="80%"}

## Why we split the roles

![Congress separates lawmaking from enforcement](../../assets/congress_breaks.jfif){fig-alt="Contrast of fused royal power with separated American branches" width="85%"}

## Concentrated force

![Illustration of abusive or concentrated power](../../assets/abuse_of_power.jpg){fig-alt="Visual cue for abuse of concentrated power"}

The executive is where coercive force is **used**, not just authorized.

## Enforcement is a choice

Which laws get priority.

Which cases get pursued.

Which emergencies get declared.

## The purse still binds

![Power of the purse constraining the executive](../../assets/the_purse.jfif){fig-alt="Illustration of executive power constrained without appropriations" width="80%"}

## Other brakes

- Senate advice and consent
- Impeachment
- Courts
- Elections
- Four-year term and the 22nd Amendment

## Last personal check

Impeachment: House charges, Senate tries.

Removal is the ultimate personal limit on the executive.

## Texas note — plural executive

![Texas plural executive](../../assets/plural_exec.jfif){fig-alt="Diagram of the Texas plural executive" width="80%"}

Texas splits executive power on purpose: suspicion of a single statewide officer.

## Recap

- We need an executive to make rights real
- Concentrated force is the standing risk
- Faithful execution is the job description
- Congress, courts, and elections are the brakes

## Top Hat

- T/F: The Take Care Clause requires the President to execute the laws Congress has made.
- MC: Hamilton's argument for a single executive emphasized:
- Likert: “A strong president is more often a defender of rights than a threat to them.”
